correctness.rationale: Every shortest accepted run is simple; in a transition-bipartite graph, any repeated-state subrun has even length, hence a first accepted word of a given parity must have a simple run. For odd n the first opposite-parity accepted word has length (t+1)n. The explicit one-cycle DFAs achieve exact length progression and have the claimed counts and correct transition parity; checker verifies 600 finite witness instances. The proof addresses all n>=2,t>=1.
